display_name: Dirty Biz XBD studio (Maelstrom-guarded netrunner hideout, Northside)
why: This is the anonymous industrial building off Shipyard Way (Watson, Northside) where XBD tuners Gottfrid and Fredrik Persson cut braindances in a small studio on the upper floor while a Maelstrom squad holds the floors below. Vanilla owns the whole site through sts_wat_nid_04 (gig Dirty Biz): the street-story prefab carries the studio set, the two BD-chair workspots and the nine-man Maelstrom community, and the always-streamed gameplay section carries the studio door, shutters, cameras and security areas. Nothing in those phases is clean-slate-kept, so the place is currently shell-only. This proposal restores the prefab and both communities in their non-hostile working phases, and switches the baked lockdown variants to the open, security-on state the studio has while it is in use. Owner decision 143: omit the two named gig tuners.

open_questions: Studio door: walk to the glass studio door and confirm it opens. It is #nid_04_dvc_studio_door; no vanilla phase drives it, so it should be a plain passable door, but it is outside DoorScope and the runtime door policy cannot fix it.

Street entrance: confirm the building's ground-floor entrance is passable. The devices prefab holds a double door and a single_door_1, but neither has an authored ref in any extract, so I could not report them as door notes.

Shutter and window look: check the studio from the street and from inside. The proposal asserts lockdown=0 / lockdown_window=0 (shutters up, normal window); if the windows still read as boarded or sealed, the lockdown variant groups mean the opposite of what I inferred and the two toggles should be flipped.

Guard posts: confirm all nine Maelstrom stand at their routine spots (ground-floor pair, upper-floor post and the Grad sniper at z~15 per the spot coords) and none spawns inside geometry or up in the studio with the tuners.
Tuners: confirm Fredrik and Gottfrid are lying in the BD chairs, jacked in, not standing (conscious) or kneeling (cower). Their chairs are #nid_04_ws_fredrik_bd and #nid_04_ws_gottfrid_bd.

Security set: confirm the cameras and security areas from #loc_sts_wat_nid_04_netrunner_hideout_devices are present and neutral (no DANGEROUS/RESTRICTED lockdown, no instant combat) with security_variant=1.

communities.why: The Maelstrom detail that holds the building for the tuners: nine entries (rifle, shotgun, machete security officer, one fast sniper with a Grad) whose only phase is default, on routine workspots - stand ground, phone call, tablet use, wall lean and two patrol stands. That is a posted guard detail, not a combat scene, so it keeps the venue occupied without a firefight. Combat groups come before civilians per rule 11a, and civilians are still included because they are the venue's reason to exist.

variant_toggles.why: The state vanilla shows once the studio is live: shutters up (lockdown off) and the security set on. The venue's own prestate phase only ever pairs lockdown=0 with security_variant=1, and the ungated boot state it writes is the closed variant (lockdown=1, security=0). Restoring 0/1 makes the den read as an operating, guarded studio instead of a sealed room. This is the devices prefab in the always-streamed gameplay section, so the toggle works at boot (rule 5).

Keeps the exterior window in its normal (non-lockdown) state. Vanilla writes lockdown_window=0 in every ungated path (openworld, prestate boot, district phase) and only sets 1 inside the gated lockdown move, so 0 is the day-to-day look and is safe to assert explicitly at boot.

proximity_wait.why: The studio's own glass door device (single_door_glass, authored name) inside the venue's always-streamed #loc_sts_wat_nid_04_netrunner_hideout_devices prefab - the only door or terminal at this venue with an authored ref. It is the natural arrival point: the studio, the two BD chairs and the upper-floor guard posts are all within ~60 m of it. This ref is not in input.json devices because no vanilla phase drives it, so the checker warns; the sector extract proves it exists as a device entity.
